title: Guess the Landmark
notes: Landmark photos are stored in the repository as locally optimized WebP files so gameplay does not fetch each photo from Wikimedia Commons.
Each image retains its sourcePage, sourceUrl, cachedSourceUrl, creator, and license metadata. If sourceUrl changes, the cache refreshes the local WebP.
Photo rendering in the published GitHub Pages site must still be checked before questions are marked approved.

questions.explanation: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 Exposition Universelle in Paris.
The Taj Mahal in Agra was commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.
Rome's Colosseum is an ancient amphitheatre used for public spectacles, including gladiatorial contests.
Known as Al-Khazneh, the Treasury is one of Petra's best-known rock-cut monuments in Jordan; its original purpose is debated.

questions.explanation: Designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon, the Sydney Opera House opened in 1973.
Angkor Wat in Cambodia began as a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu and later became a Buddhist religious site.
Christ the Redeemer is the large Art Deco statue atop Corcovado mountain overlooking Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa is the cathedral's freestanding bell tower; its tilt began because of an inadequate foundation on soft ground.
Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca site set high in the Peruvian Andes, surrounded by steep mountain slopes and terraces.
The Parthenon is the famous temple on Athens' Acropolis, built in the 5th century BCE and dedicated to Athena.
Mount Rushmore in South Dakota features the carved faces of four U.S. presidents: George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln.
The Golden Gate Bridge spans the entrance to San Francisco Bay and opened to vehicle traffic in May 1937.
The Forbidden City in Beijing was the imperial palace of China's Ming and Qing dynasties for centuries.
Big Ben is the nickname of the Great Bell inside the Elizabeth Tower at the Palace of Westminster in London.
The moai are monumental stone figures carved by the Rapa Nui people on Rapa Nui, also known as Easter Island.
